newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-TYSON LOSES LAWSUIT TO FORMER TRAINER.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-TYSON LOSES LAWSUIT TO FORMER TRAINER.

text.p: A federal jury Monday awarded Kevin Rooney, Mike Tyson's former trainer, $4.1 million and said the heavyweight boxing champion did not have just cause when he fired him in 1988.
Rooney, who sought $49 million in the lawsuit, did not win claims to any of the projected future earnings by the fighter.

Tyson, whose presence drew hundreds of supporters to the Albany federal courthouse, described the verdict as "ridiculous" and said, "if Kevin would have asked me for $4 million dollars I would have given it to him."

In the lawsuit Rooney accused the boxer of failing to honour a verbal contract made to him by Tyson's late mentor Cus D'Amato, promising him a lifetime job with a guaranteed 10 percent cut of the boxer's winnings.
Tyson's fortune was estimated at $490 million.
Tyson's attorney argued that the boxer knew nothing about such a contract. D'Amato died in 1985.
"I'm satisfied," Rooney told reporters. "I never expected $49 million but you can't take blood from a stone. They came in with what they feel is a just verdict and I'm not going to argue with it."
The jury found that Rooney proved he had an employment contract and proved that the employment relationship was of a definite duration.

It said Rooney proved he had performed obligations under the contract at the time he was fired and found Tyson did not prove he had just cause to fire Rooney over the trainer's public comments about Tyson's failed marriage to actress Robin Givens.
Rooney worked with Tyson from his amateur days in 1982 until 1988 when he was world champion.

The trial was postponed by Tyson's conviction in 1992 and prison sentence for the rape of Desiree Washington, a 19-year-old beauty contestant. He was paroled in March 1995 and has won four bouts without a loss since then.
After the verdict, which the jury reached in just under 10 hours, Tyson supporters chanted "no justice no peace" and promoter Don King said the boxer's rights had been infringed.

"I have no problem with an all-white jury," King said. "I have a problem when rights are eroded. You took away a man's rights. This was a dead man's contract and it enslaved Mike Tyson. This is what divides us, this kind of racism, white and black alike."
